title: JobRequest
description: What an editor asked for. Written by the panel, consumed by the helper, which runs the engine and returns an EditPlan. Closed to unknown keys: a typo here would otherwise silently fall back to a default and produce the wrong edit.

jobId.description: Also used for the sequence name and the output filename, so it must be filesystem-safe.

requestedBy.description: Free text, for shared job folders.

media.description: Paths relative to the media root, matching how EditPlan stores them.

aspect.description: 'source' keeps the footage's own shape and skips reframing entirely.

frameRate.description: Sequence frame rate. 'auto' follows the recipe and the footage; otherwise a rate such as '25', '29.97', '59.94' or '30000/1001'. Above 60 is refused: Premiere will not create the sequence.

mode.description: upTo: fill and stop. exactly: trim the last clip to land on it. about: rank and trim within tolerance, never force.

pacing.description: Scales the recipe's timing values rather than replacing them, so the recipe stays the editorial source of truth.

look.description: Key into brandkit luts, or null for no grade.

music.description: 'auto' to find a single audio-only file beside the footage, 'none' to skip, or a path relative to the media root.

musicChunk.description: Which part of the track to use. A trend is a moment in a song, not its opening. Omitting lengthSeconds keeps the bed following the picture; setting it lays that much music even past the last frame.

startSeconds.description: Seconds into the track to start.

lengthSeconds.description: Seconds of track to use. Omit to follow the picture.

snapToBeat.description: Move the start to the nearest beat. Shot lengths are already whole multiples of the beat interval, so starting the bed on a beat phase-aligns the whole cut grid to what is audible.

visual.description: Cut from the pictures even when the footage has usable audio.

subtitles.description: Write an .srt for the finished edit. A speech edit already has the words; a montage does not, so this makes it transcribe for subtitles alone.

protectSpeech.description: Never cut through the middle of what someone is saying: a boundary landing inside an utterance moves to its edge. Implied by subtitles.

removeSilence.description: Trim silence beyond silenceAllowed from each take, and drop takes with no speech in them.

silenceAllowed.description: Seconds of silence to leave around what is said. Only meaningful with removeSilence.

story.description: The video described in plain text. Its beats become the running order, matched against what is actually in the footage. Implies visual cutting: beats are matched against pictures, so there is nothing to match without them. A beat nothing matches is left out and named in a warning rather than filled with the nearest thing.

reference.description: Cut the footage to match this video's structure -- its shot count, its shot lengths and their order. The reference is measured and discarded; no frame of it reaches the timeline. A description, when one is given, wins over it.

source.description: 'file' is a path relative to the reference folder; 'url' is a link the helper downloads once and caches.

matchContent.description: Also try to match what each reference shot shows, not only how long it runs. When nothing matches, the rhythm is used on its own and that is reported.

model.description: Transcription model override, e.g. small or large-v3.

cutRate.description: Beats per shot when the music leads. Below 1 subdivides: 0.5 also cuts halfway between beats, which stays right as the tempo drifts because it is the midpoint of two ACTUAL beats. Omit to follow `pacing`.
